## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the determination of dissolved organic carbon
(DOC) in natural water samples (surface water, groundwater,
stormwater, treated effluent) by the non-purgeable organic carbon
(NPOC) method on the Shimadzu TOC-L analyzer. DOC is a fundamental
water quality parameter that influences aquatic ecosystem productivity,
light penetration, metal complexation, disinfection byproduct
formation, and nutrient cycling [@thurman1985; @wetzel2001].

The NPOC method acidifies the sample and sparges with carrier gas to
remove inorganic carbon (CO~2~, HCO~3~^-^, CO~3~^2-^) before
combustion. The remaining carbon is measured as NPOC, which for most
natural waters is operationally equivalent to DOC when the sample has
been filtered through 0.45 um [@apha2012, Section 5310B].

For instrument operation, startup, and shutdown, see
[SOP-L204 Shimadzu TOC-L](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd). For
water-extractable DOC from soils, see
[SOP-L418](SOP-L418-water-extractable-doc.qmd).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Filtered (0.45 um) water samples from surface water,
  groundwater, stormwater, effluent, and precipitation, analyzed for
  DOC in NPOC mode on the Shimadzu TOC-L
- **Does not apply to:** Total organic carbon in unfiltered water (use
  TOC mode on the TOC-L); particulate organic carbon (requires
  separate filtration and combustion); soil carbon by SSM (see
  [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd)); soil extract DOC (see
  [SOP-L418](SOP-L418-water-extractable-doc.qmd)); microbial biomass
  carbon (see [SOP-L409](SOP-L409-microbial-biomass-carbon.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program analytical laboratory, SGM 133

| Role               | Responsibility                                         |
|:-------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI             | Approve protocol, ensure training compliance           |
| Instrument Manager | Maintain the TOC-L per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) |
| Trained Personnel  | Prepare samples and standards, run analysis, export data |
| New Students       | Complete training before independent use               |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

All safety requirements from
[SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) Section 4 apply.
Additional hazards specific to this method:

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Hydrochloric acid (2 M HCl) is used for sample
  acidification and preservation. Avoid skin and eye contact.
- **Glassware:** Pre-combusted glass vials are fragile. Handle with
  care to avoid cuts.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves


## 5. Required Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Shimadzu TOC-L with ASI-L autosampler | Operated per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) |
| TNM-L (optional)                      | If simultaneous TN analysis is desired |
| Vacuum filtration apparatus           | Per [SOP-L114](SOP-L114-vacuum-filtration.qmd) |
| Analytical balance (0.001 g)          | Per [SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd) |

### Consumables

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Pre-combusted glass vials (40 mL, with PTFE-lined caps) | Combust at 450 C for 4 hours per [SOP-L111](SOP-L111-muffle-furnace.qmd); or purchase pre-combusted |
| Autosampler vials (8 mL or 40 mL)    | Pre-combusted or acid-washed   |
| 0.45 um filters (PVDF or PES)        | Do NOT use cellulose acetate (leaches DOC) [@kaplan1994] |
| Syringe filters (0.45 um, 25 mm)     | PVDF; discard first 2--3 mL of filtrate |
| Graduated pipettes or micropipettes  | For acid and standard additions |

### Reagents

| Reagent                               | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| KHP stock standard (1,000 mg C/L)     | 2.125 g KHP per 1 L DI water; prepare fresh monthly; store at 4 C [@apha2012] |
| 2 M HCl (Trace Metal grade)          | For sample acidification       |
| Deionized water (18.2 MOhm)          | From Milli-Q; verify DOC less than 0.05 mg/L |

::: {.callout-important}
Prepare the 1,000 mg C/L KHP stock solution fresh monthly or verify
against a certified reference material (CRM) before use. Degraded
stock causes a systematic low bias across the calibration.
:::


## 6. Sample Collection and Preservation

Proper sample handling is critical for DOC; contamination from fingers,
plastic containers, and atmospheric CO~2~ can bias results
[@sharp1993].

| Parameter           | Requirement                                     |
|:--------------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| Container           | Pre-combusted amber glass (40 mL) with PTFE-lined cap; or acid-washed HDPE if glass is not available |
| Filtration          | Filter through 0.45 um within 24 hours of collection; PVDF or PES membrane (not cellulose acetate) |
| Preservation        | Acidify to pH less than 2 with 2 M HCl (approximately 2 drops per 40 mL) immediately after filtration |
| Storage             | 4 C in the dark                                 |
| Holding time        | 28 days from collection (acidified) [@apha2012] |

::: {.callout-note}
For field collection procedures, see
[SOP-F300 Surface Water Sampling](../field_sops/SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd).
Bottles for DOC should be filled with minimal headspace to reduce
CO~2~ exchange.
:::


## 7. Procedure

### 7.1 Preparing Calibration Standards

1. From the 1,000 mg C/L KHP stock, prepare a working calibration
   series by serial dilution with deionized water. A typical series
   for natural water DOC:

   | Standard | Concentration (mg C/L) |
   |:---------|:----------------------:|
   | Blank    | 0                      |
   | S1       | 0.5                    |
   | S2       | 1.0                    |
   | S3       | 2.5                    |
   | S4       | 5.0                    |
   | S5       | 10.0                   |
   | S6       | 25.0                   |
   | S7       | 50.0                   |

2. Prepare standards in pre-combusted glass volumetric flasks. Rinse
   each flask 3 times with deionized water before use.
3. Transfer standards to autosampler vials. Acidify each standard
   with 2 M HCl to match the sample matrix (same acid volume per
   volume as the samples).

::: {.callout-tip}
For low-DOC samples (less than 5 mg/L, typical of oligotrophic lakes
and groundwater), use only the 0--10 mg/L range and omit the 25 and
50 mg/L standards. A narrower range improves precision at low
concentrations.
:::

### 7.2 Preparing Samples

1. If samples were not filtered in the field, filter through 0.45 um
   PVDF syringe filters into pre-combusted glass vials. Discard the
   first 2--3 mL of filtrate (filter blank rinse).
2. Verify that samples have been acidified to pH less than 2. If not
   previously acidified, add 2 M HCl dropwise until pH paper
   indicates pH less than 2 (typically 2--4 drops per 40 mL).
3. Allow acidified samples to reach room temperature before loading
   into the autosampler (cold samples produce air bubbles in the
   syringe).
4. Transfer samples to autosampler vials if they are not already in
   compatible vials. Fill to the level specified in the autosampler
   manual (typically at least 10 mL for a 40 mL vial position, or
   5 mL for an 8 mL position).

### 7.3 Instrument Setup

1. Start the TOC-L per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd)
   Section 7.1 or 7.2 (cold start or from standby)
2. In the Method Editor, set:
   - **Measurement mode:** NPOC
   - **Injection volume:** 50 uL (default; adjust if needed)
   - **Number of injections:** 3 minimum (set maximum to 5 with
     automatic outlier exclusion)
   - **Sparge time:** 1.5 minutes (default; increase to 3 minutes for
     high-alkalinity samples with IC above 50 mg/L)
   - **Acidification:** Automatic, using the IC reagent (25% H~3~PO~4~)
     dispensed by the instrument. The instrument adds a fixed volume
     (typically 15 uL of 2 M HCl equivalent) to each injection.
3. If TN is also being measured, confirm TN is enabled in the Method
   Editor

### 7.4 Sample Table and Run Sequence

Enter the following sequence in the Sample Table:

| Position | Sample Type                 | Notes                          |
|:---------|:----------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| 1--3     | Deionized water blanks      | System conditioning (discard results) |
| 4--6     | Deionized water blanks      | Reported blanks; must be less than 0.1 mg/L C |
| 7        | Calibration verification (mid-range, e.g., 5 mg/L) | Recovery must be 90--110% |
| 8--14    | Calibration standards (low to high) | Build the calibration curve |
| 15       | Method blank (if applicable) | E.g., DI water acidified with the same HCl used for samples |
| 16--25   | Samples                     | In order of loading             |
| 26       | Continuing calibration verification (CCV) | Every 10--15 samples; 5 or 10 mg/L |
| 27       | Deionized water blank       | Monitor for carryover           |
| 28--37   | Samples                     | Continue                        |
| 38       | CCV                         | End-of-run verification         |
| 39--41   | Deionized water blanks      | Final system flush              |

### 7.5 Running the Analysis

1. Load all vials into the autosampler, verifying that rack positions
   match the Sample Table
2. Confirm the ASI-L rinse reservoir is full
3. Click **Start**
4. Monitor the first few injections to verify normal peak shape and
   baseline stability
5. The run proceeds unattended; the autosampler advances automatically

### 7.6 Data Review and Export

1. After the run, open the Data Browser
2. Check each result:
   - Replicate injection CV must be less than 2%
   - Blank values must be less than 0.1 mg/L C (flag run if higher)
   - CCV recovery must be 90--110%; if it drifts outside this range,
     re-calibrate and re-run affected samples
3. If a sample exceeds the calibration range, dilute and re-run
4. Export results to CSV per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd)
   Section 7.9
5. Record the run in the instrument logbook


## 8. Calculations

The TOC-L software reports NPOC concentration directly in mg C/L,
corrected for dilution factor if entered in the Sample Table. For
reporting as DOC:

$$
\text{DOC (mg C/L)} = \text{NPOC}_{\text{reported}} - \text{NPOC}_{\text{method blank}}
$$

If samples were diluted before analysis, apply the dilution factor:

$$
\text{DOC (mg C/L)} = (\text{NPOC}_{\text{reported}} - \text{NPOC}_{\text{blank}}) \times D
$$

where $D$ is the dilution factor (e.g., 2 for a 1:1 dilution).

### R Code for Batch Processing

```{r}
#| label: doc-npoc-calc
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# ===========================================================================
# SOP-L311: DOC (NPOC) -- Batch calculation from TOC-L CSV export
# ===========================================================================

# ---- 1. Read the TOC-L CSV export ----------------------------------------
# Adjust the filename and column names to match your LabSolutions export
raw <- read.csv("TOC-L_export.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Expected columns (rename as needed):
#   SampleID, NPOC_mg_L, CV_pct, Dilution

# ---- 2. Identify blanks and CCV ------------------------------------------
blanks <- raw[grepl("^Blank|^DI|^MQ", raw$SampleID, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
ccv    <- raw[grepl("^CCV|^CVS|^Check", raw$SampleID, ignore.case = TRUE), ]

mean_blank <- mean(blanks$NPOC_mg_L, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("Mean method blank: %.3f mg C/L\n", mean_blank))
cat(sprintf("CCV recoveries: %s\n",
            paste(sprintf("%.1f%%",
                          ccv$NPOC_mg_L / ccv$Dilution * 100),
                  collapse = ", ")))

# ---- 3. Calculate blank-corrected DOC ------------------------------------
samples <- raw[!grepl("^Blank|^DI|^MQ|^CCV|^CVS|^Check|^Std",
                       raw$SampleID, ignore.case = TRUE), ]

samples$DOC_mg_L <- (samples$NPOC_mg_L - mean_blank) * samples$Dilution
samples$DOC_mg_L[samples$DOC_mg_L < 0] <- 0

# ---- 4. Flag QC issues ---------------------------------------------------
samples$QC_flag <- ""
samples$QC_flag[samples$CV_pct > 2] <- "CV>2%"

cat("\nResults:\n")
print(samples[, c("SampleID", "NPOC_mg_L", "Dilution",
                   "DOC_mg_L", "QC_flag")],
      row.names = FALSE)
```


## 9. Quality Control

### 9.1 Instrument QC

Per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) Section 8:

- System blanks less than 0.1 mg/L C
- Calibration r^2^ at least 0.999
- Replicate injection CV less than 2%
- CCV recovery 90--110%

### 9.2 Method QC

| QC Element                    | Frequency            | Acceptance Criteria            |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Method blank (acidified DI)   | 1 per batch          | Less than 0.2 mg/L C           |
| Field blank (from SOP-F300)   | 1 per sampling event | Less than 0.5 mg/L C           |
| Laboratory duplicate          | 1 per 10 samples     | RPD less than 10%              |
| Certified reference material  | 1 per batch (when available) | Recovery 90--110%       |
| Matrix spike                  | 1 per 20 samples     | Recovery 80--120%              |

### 9.3 Common Contamination Sources

DOC is easily contaminated. The most common sources and their
prevention [@kaplan1994; @sharp1993]:

| Source                        | Prevention                                |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Fingers touching vial interiors | Always wear gloves; handle vials by the exterior only |
| Cellulose acetate filters     | Use PVDF or PES filters exclusively       |
| Detergent residue on glassware | Use pre-combusted glass; or acid-wash and rinse with DI |
| Atmospheric CO~2~ absorption  | Minimize headspace in vials; cap immediately |
| Degraded DI water             | Verify DI water DOC less than 0.05 mg/L before each session |
| Old or degraded KHP stock     | Prepare fresh monthly; refrigerate        |


## 10. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Acidified sample waste        | Neutralize and drain, or collect per [SOP-L006](SOP-L006-waste-disposal.qmd) |
| Calibration standard waste    | Drain (dilute KHP, non-hazardous)        |
| Used syringe filters          | Standard trash                           |
| Pre-combusted glass vials     | Rinse and reuse, or glass recycling      |

## 13. Training Record

Before performing this analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete instrument training per
   [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) Section 14
3. Demonstrate competence preparing KHP calibration standards
4. Demonstrate proper sample filtration technique (PVDF filter, first-
   rinse discard)
5. Perform a supervised DOC run with acceptable QC results (blanks,
   CCV, duplicate RPD)
6. Process one batch through the R calculation code and verify results
   against the LabSolutions export
7. Be signed off by the instrument manager or PI
